110303001.accepts_evidence: Donor-advised fund sponsor. Its FAQ for nonprofits says it does not accept applications for funding; every grant is recommended by a donor from that donor's Giving Account, and nonprofits are told to work with donors directly. Donor-advised grants cannot be applied for. https://www.fidelitycharitable.org/nonprofits/nonprofits-frequently-asked-questions.html
110303001.contact: Nonprofit service team 800-952-4438 (prompt 4), Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. ET
110303001.eligibility: Recipients must generally be IRS-qualified 501(c)(3) public charities and each recommendation must meet the program guidelines; supporting organizations have separate rules.
110303001.geographic_limits: not stated (grants go wherever donors recommend)
110303001.how_to_apply: There is no application. A nonprofit can make itself easy to find and pay: keep its public name matched to its IRS name, show its tax ID on its website, add the DAF Direct widget, and enroll for electronic payment (Stripe or ACH, both free) instead of mailed checks.
110303001.name: Fidelity Charitable (Fidelity Investments Charitable Gift Fund)
110303001.not_funded: Applications of any kind. No competitive program is described on the nonprofit FAQ.
110303001.notes: Not a prospect to apply to. A Fidelity Charitable grant on a peer's donor list means an individual donor with a Giving Account chose that organization; the cultivation target is the donor. Search results mentioned a Trustees' Initiative and a Catalyst Fund run by Fidelity Charitable itself; those pages were not read, and the nonprofit FAQ lists no open program.
110303001.page_dated: Copyright 1998-2026; cites 2025 totals ($18.3 billion to nearly 227,000 charities)
priorities: None of its own - grants follow each donor's recommendation

111694718.accepts_evidence: All prospective grantees must first submit a Letter of Inquiry through the foundation's Submittable portal during a set window; only selected applicants are invited to send a full application (https://sfoa.org/prospective-grantees/).
111694718.conflicts_with_return: none (return lists deadlines as N/A, while the site runs three dated LOI windows a year; both show an open route)
111694718.contact: info@sfoa.org; (646) 854-9975; 3 Columbus Circle, 15th Floor, New York, NY 10019
111694718.deadlines: 2027 Cycle 1 (end of life care / elder neglect): LOI window closed; invitations late October 2026; awards February 2027. 2027 Cycle 2 (dementia care): LOI opens Monday November 16, 2026 and closes Thursday December 17, 2026 at 5pm ET; invitations early March 2027; awards June 2027. 2027 Cycle 3 (social isolation): LOI opens Thursday March 18, 2027 and closes Tuesday April 20, 2027 at 5pm ET; invitations June 2027; awards September 2027.
111694718.eligibility: 501(c)(3) nonprofit or an organization with a 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor; operating for at least two years
111694718.geographic_limits: not stated (home page describes work for older people around the world; no grant region given)
111694718.how_to_apply: Submit a Letter of Inquiry in Submittable during the window for the matching focus area. If invited, send a full application with audited financials, latest Form 990, IRS determination letter and organization (and project) budget.
111694718.name: Sephardic Foundation on Aging
111694718.not_funded: Individuals, endowments, colleges and universities, political organizations or action groups, debt reduction, multi-year proposals
111694718.notes: Three themed LOI cycles a year, each tied to one focus area, so apply in the cycle that fits. The dementia care LOI window opens November 16, 2026. Originated as the Sephardic Home for the Aged in Brooklyn; the pages read do not say grants are limited to Sephardic or Jewish organizations. The return gives a staff email for applications; the site publishes only the general info address.
111694718.page_dated: Prospective Grantees page last modified September 17, 2026; footer copyright 2026
priorities: end of life care and preventing or addressing elder neglect (Cycle 1)
dementia care and degenerative brain diseases (Cycle 2)
combating social isolation of older adults (Cycle 3)
capital improvements for nursing care facilities
111694718.types_of_support: not stated on the grantee page; home page mentions program support and funding for construction, renovation and major equipment at care facilities; no multi-year grants

113276603.accepts_evidence: Capital One's community page says grant requests under its Community Benefits Plan are taken only by invitation, with partners found through ongoing relationship building by local leaders and current partners; an open call or RFP may be used in select cases (https://www.capitalone.com/about/community/). The page speaks for Capital One's community giving as a whole and does not name the Foundation.
113276603.confidence: medium - the company page describes Capital One's grant process without naming the Foundation as a separate funder
113276603.contact: not stated (the page says intake details would be published later)
113276603.geographic_limits: not stated (mostly locally driven work in Capital One markets, plus select national partners)
113276603.how_to_apply: No open route. Funding is by invitation, decided case by case on fit with the plan's goals; watch for occasional open calls or RFPs announced by Capital One.
113276603.name: Capital One Foundation Inc
113276603.notes: Corporate foundation with no site of its own; its giving sits inside Capital One's community programs. The current frame is a five-year Community Benefits Plan (2025-2029). One past open call was a $25M homeownership call that has already named finalists. A 2020 newsroom item shows the pattern of grants of about $500,000 to local nonprofits in Dallas, New Orleans, New York, Richmond and Washington, D.C.; that is old and given only as background.
113276603.page_dated: Page reports progress for July to December 2025 and says annual updates begin Q2 2026; footer copyright 2026
